## Summary of the Patch

The patch fixes a use-after-free bug in `ksmbd_open()` (in `fs/smb/server/smb2pdu.c`) that occurred during durable handle reconnection when error handling paths or a scavenger accessed the file pointer (`fp`) after it had already been released.

### Modifications in `fs/smb/server/smb2pdu.c`

**Removed calls** (four occurrences inside the `if (dh_info.reconnected)` block):
- `ksmbd_put_durable_fd(dh_info.fp)` after `smb2_check_durable_oplock()` failure (line ~3018).
- `ksmbd_put_durable_fd(dh_info.fp)` after `ksmbd_reopen_durable_fd()` failure (line ~3022).
- `ksmbd_put_durable_fd(dh_info.fp)` after `ksmbd_override_fsids()` failure (line ~3027).
- `ksmbd_put_durable_fd(fp)` after `ksmbd_vfs_getattr()` (line ~3031). (Note: `fp` equals `dh_info.fp`.)

**Added call** (at the end of the function, after `err_out2` label, before `kfree` statements):
- `if (dh_info.reconnected) ksmbd_put_durable_fd(dh_info.fp);`

### Relationship of the Modifications

The early `ksmbd_put_durable_fd()` calls were prematurely dropping the reference to the durable file descriptor. Any subsequent error (e.g., `ksmbd_iov_pin_rsp` failure) or external access (e.g., by a scavenger) would then operate on freed memory, causing a use-after-free. By removing those early releases and moving a single release to the very end of the function (outside all error handling that might still need `fp`), the patch ensures that `fp` remains valid until `smb2_open()` fully returns. This effectively consolidates multiple early puts into one late put, preserving the reference count throughout the critical section.
